messages.subject: Re: about ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
# Prepare the data and library
rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)
probgrp <- read.table("probgrp.txt", header=T)

# Show the default ordering (alphanumerically)
sort(as.character(probgrp$ItemValue))

# Re-ordering it save as ItemValue2. This might be what you want.
probgrp$ItemValue2 <- factor(probgrp$ItemValue, levels=probgrp$ItemValue)

# Plot the figure
p <- ggplot(probgrp, aes(x=ItemValue2, y=Probability,group=1))+
  geom_line(col="red",size=2)+geom_point(col="darkred",size=3)
print(p)

>   我打了 chisq(10,0.95) 卻顯示錯誤: 沒有這個函數 "chisq"
>   我想請問是我誤會題目的意思 還是chi-squared 是別種代號??
>
>
> 2,If you create a variable using the following command y=c(-1,2,-3,4,-5),what command would put the positive values of y into the variable z?
>    它的意思是要我把y的column 都加絕對值變成Z嗎?? 還是題目問的是別的事情??
>
> 謝謝各位的解答

卡方有这个函数 chisq()
可以help(chisq)查看 文档

chisq 卡方 的变量 是x^2  你输入负数的话是不对的；
所以提醒你改成Positive

messages.subject: 關於3D繪圖
messages.body_plain:
關於3D繪圖 下面的函數想要建立一個概似函數 再跑出他的3D圖
但是發現 在
sum(y^2)+6*(b0^2)+(b1^2)*sum(x^2)+2*b0*b1*sum(x)-2*b0*sum(y)-2*b1*sum(x*y)是可以跑出3D圖的 但如果採用 矩陣的表示 t(y-b1*x-b0)%*%(y-b1*x-b0)
會出現長度不對的訊息 明明解都是一樣的 用 [1] 抓數字出來也不能跑 有高手可以幫解惑嗎?

read.table("D:/data3.txt")
data=read.table("D:/data3.txt")
x=data[,2]
y=data[,1]

b0=seq(-10,10,length=30)
b1=seq(17,19,length=30)

likelihood=function(b0,b1)
{
 ((2*pi*16)^(-6/2))*exp(-((2*16)^(-1))*(sum(y^2)+6*(b0^2)+(b1^2)*sum(x^2)+2*b0*b1*sum(x)-2*b0*sum(y)-2*b1*sum(x*y)))

}

z=outer(b0,b1,likelihood)
persp(b0,b1,z, theta = 75, phi = 30, expand = 0.5, col = "green",
ltheta = 90, shade = 0.75, ticktype = "detailed",
xlab = "b0", ylab = "b1", zlab = "Likelihood")

data3.txt 內容 128.0 7.0
213.0 12.0
75.0 4.0
250.0 14.0
446.0 25.0
540.0 30.0

messages.body_plain:
Most people with least programming skill don't need any kind of books like "R for beginers" at all.
As a programming language, R is extremely easy, a reference card and some examples are enough for all kind of users.
http://www.mayin.org/ajayshah/KB/R/
http://cran.r-project.org/doc/contrib/Baggott-refcard-v2.pdf
For searching packages, there's CRAN Task Views <http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/> and RSeek <http://www.rseek.org/>.

What I meant in previous post was something like "healthcare statistics".
Although I don't know anything about healthcare,  but stats is generally about collecting data, pre-processing data, applying appropriate models to specific data and validating.
As an example, this paper <http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/project/seermed/paper/pap033104.pdf> mentioned some models and validation methods. Look out what they used, research why the thing they used works and attempt something new. There's a lot of packages you can find in CRAN.
